text: I opened the bakery in '98. Back then the street was all families. Now it's coffee places and the council keeps raising my rent, and I just keep my head down.
Going on thirty years I have lived on this street. My kids went to the old school on Hale Road. They closed it. Now it's flats nobody I know can afford.
We moved in last spring. Honestly it's lovely, the cafés, the little park. The neighbours were a bit cold at first but that's changing.
I own four of the houses on Lark Lane. The bank wanted a renovation before the next loan, so yes, I raised the rents. It is business.
I haven't lived here long enough to say what it was like before. Ask the old man at number nine.
Born here, forty-one years. The police patrol more now, which is good, but they stop my son every second week. Is that safety?
My shop sells shoes. Since the new tram stop, footfall doubled. The council did something right for once. I am proud of this street.
I came here in 2015 with two suitcases. The housing association gave us a flat. Now they say the building will be sold. Where do we go?
Twelve years I have run the laundrette. Nothing has changed except the prices on the menu next door.
The school here is finally getting a new roof and the library reopens in March. I think the next ten years will be better than the last.
Used to be everyone knew everyone. My grandmother's house is now a dentist's. I still walk past it every Sunday.
Nine months in. The landlord ignored the mould for six of them, and the council inspector never showed. I am done.
